jobs.title: The unprinted year, i
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 23, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands in its pockets, plain tee, dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Three weeks without a reader. The line is already looser. A strip about nothing — the dog, the fan, the heat — drawn as if someone would see it, which nobody will. Panel 1: brush-pen black-and-white, looser line than usual, a young man on a bedroom floor with a pad and a dog lying flat in front of a box fan with its ears blowing (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 2: brush-pen black-and-white, loose, close-up of a dog's face in front of a fan with its ears and jowls blown back (in this panel: BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 3: brush-pen black-and-white, loose, a young man sliding a dog sideways away from a fan and the dog sliding back, no words (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 4: brush-pen black-and-white, loose fat line, a young man and a dog side by side in front of a box fan with hair and ears blowing, a blank pad on the floor (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No text, no lettering, no speech balloons, no signature; leave clean space in each panel where balloons would go. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
